Job Description

At Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), we are building the next generation of cloud services for autonomous and intelligent robotics.

OCI Robotics Cloud is Oracle's strategic cloud platform for robotics. Our mission is to enable enterprises to seamlessly onboard, manage, monitor, and operate heterogeneous robot fleets through secure, scalable, AI-powered cloud services.

Unlike traditional robotics platforms that focus on individual robots, OCI Robotics Cloud is building the cloud operating system for robotics—providing common services for robot identity, registration, fleet management, mission orchestration, telemetry, digital twins, software lifecycle management, and AI-powered automation.

A key part of our vision is an AI-driven, spec-based robot onboarding platform
that enables robots from any vendor to integrate rapidly through standardized cloud interfaces, reusable edge services, and AI-generated service contracts.

As Director of OCI Robotics Cloud, you will build both the platform and the organization that will define Oracle's long-term robotics strategy.

This is a rare opportunity to build a greenfield cloud platform with executive visibility and industry-wide impact at the intersection of AI, cloud infrastructure, robotics, and edge computing.

Responsibilities

About You

You are a builder.

You enjoy creating organizations, platforms, and engineering cultures from the ground up.

You have successfully led engineering teams building large-scale cloud platforms and understand how to balance long-term technical vision with rapid execution.

You believe great platforms are built around reusable abstractions, developer productivity, and operational excellence.

You are passionate about AI and understand how generative AI can fundamentally improve software engineering, developer experience, and platform automation.

You have a proven track record of hiring, mentoring, and growing exceptional engineering organizations.

You communicate effectively with engineers, architects, product leaders, customers, and executive leadership.

What You'll Do

Define the Platform

Define the long-term architecture and technical vision for OCI Robotics Cloud.
Build the cloud platform enabling robot registration, identity, fleet management, mission orchestration, telemetry, digital twins, and software lifecycle management.
Establish common APIs, service contracts, SDKs, and edge service frameworks that support robots from multiple vendors.

Lead AI-driven Engineering

Lead the development of an AI-assisted, spec-driven robot onboarding platform where AI generates service contracts, edge service specifications, SDKs, implementation guidance, and developer documentation.
Drive adoption of AI throughout the software development lifecycle to improve engineering productivity and platform quality.

Build the Organization

Recruit, mentor, and grow a world-class cloud engineering organization.
Build a culture centered on engineering excellence, ownership, customer obsession, and continuous innovation.
Coach engineering managers and senior technical leaders while developing future organizational leadership.

Deliver at Scale

Drive engineering execution across architecture, planning, prioritization, delivery, reliability, security, observability, and operational excellence.
Partner closely with Product Management to define roadmap and customer adoption strategy.
Collaborate across OCI AI, Cloud Infrastructure, Security, Networking, Developer Services, and strategic robotics partners.
Represent OCI Robotics Cloud in executive reviews, customer engagements, and strategic technology initiatives.

Minimum Qualifications

BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical field.
12+ years of experience building distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, or enterprise software platforms.
5+ years of engineering management experience leading multiple software engineering teams.
Proven experience defining and delivering large-scale cloud platforms from concept to production.
Strong technical background in distributed systems, Kubernetes, APIs, microservices, cloud-native architectures, and modern software engineering practices.
Demonstrated success hiring and scaling engineering organizations.
Outstanding communication, leadership, and organizational skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with cloud robotics, IoT, autonomous systems, or edge computing platforms.
Familiarity with ROS 2 and modern robotics software architectures.
Experience with DDS, MQTT, OPC-UA, VDA5050, or related robotics communication technologies.
Experience building developer platforms, SDKs, APIs, or service contract frameworks.
Experience with AI-assisted software development, developer productivity platforms, or agentic AI systems.
Exposure to embodied AI, vision-language models, robot fleet management, digital twins, or teleoperation platforms.
Experience working with heterogeneous hardware ecosystems and partner integrations.

Why Join Us

Build Oracle's cloud platform for the next generation of intelligent robotics.
Pioneer AI-driven, spec-based robot onboarding technologies.
Define the open cloud interfaces that enable robots from any vendor to integrate with OCI.
Lead one of Oracle's newest strategic engineering organizations.
Collaborate with world-class engineers across OCI AI, Cloud Infrastructure, Security, and Developer Services.
Shape Oracle's long-term strategy for cloud robotics, AI, and autonomous systems.

Vision

Our vision is to make robot onboarding as simple as cloud onboarding.

We believe AI will fundamentally transform how robots are integrated into enterprise systems by automatically generating service contracts, edge services, SDKs, APIs, implementation guidance, and operational best practices.

OCI Robotics Cloud is building the cloud platform that allows any robot—from any vendor—to securely connect to Oracle Cloud through standardized interfaces rather than custom integrations.

As Director of OCI Robotics Cloud, you will build the engineering organization that turns this vision into reality.

You will report to our Chief Technology Officer. This role can be remote, but we have a preference for someone to be close to one of our offices in NY, NJ, or CA.

Provide technical expertise to develop core technologies that our project teams will utilize to deliver distributed energy solutions.
Leverage electrical and power engineering knowledge to define best practices and publish internal standards and guidelines to ensure high-quality microgrid projects are engineered well for our clients.
Review project-specific electrical designs and the sequence of operations for controls
Provide technical oversight and guidance on relay protection settings and power systems analysis
Define long-term technical vision and product roadmaps for microgrid design and core technologies.

Strong communication skills, including the ability to communicate with technical and non-technical people to make projects work.

About The Role

Senior Engineering Managers at GitLab own outcomes for a defined engineering domain, build and grow the team that delivers them, and are trusted to operate with significant autonomy against a clear mandate.

This Senior Engineering Manager role focuses on driving non-linear productivity by building and leading a small, hand-picked team of engineers who find and fix the highest-leverage friction points in GitLab's own SDLC. Rather than incremental team management, this is a 0 to 1 team-building mandate. You will personally recruit 4 exceptional engineers, define how they work, and drive them through a root-cause, shift-left approach to engineering productivity, measured in system-level metrics (MRPM, pipeline success rate, pipeline latency), not story points or activity.

You will act as a bridge between the pilot squad, engineering managers whose teams are affected by friction points, and leadership, ensuring the team's fixes deliver durable, measurable value before any of it is proposed as a permanent function.

This role reports to a VP-level engineering leader.

What You'll Do

Vision & Strategy

Define and continuously refine the operating model for the non-linear productivity pilot: what "friction" means, how it's diagnosed, and how fixes are prioritized against the three system-level metrics.
Identify and prioritize non-linear productivity opportunities (step-change fixes rather than incremental gains) across the SDLC, including flaky tests, review latency, pipeline reliability, tooling gaps, and context loss for both human and agentic contributors.
Translate an intentionally broad, ambiguous mandate ("find the friction, fix it at the root") into a concrete, time-boxed roadmap with defined milestones for a 3-month pilot window.

Team Building & Leadership

Personally source, evaluate, and select 4 exceptional engineers for the pilot squad. You own this hiring bar directly rather than delegating it to a pipeline.
Negotiate allocation models (100% vs. partial/dual-hat) with each engineer's current EM, balancing team commitments against the pilot's needs.
Set the technical direction and working norms for a small, fast-moving team: how work is scoped, how decisions get made, and how progress gets reported.
Mentor the engineers on this team in root-cause diagnosis and shift-left thinking, raising the bar for rigor versus reaching for the nearest patch.

Deep Technical Exploration & Experimentation

Lead hands-on investigation to instrument and baseline the three top-level metrics (MRPM, pipeline success rate, pipeline latency) so the org has an honest starting point before any fix is proposed.
Diagnose the highest-leverage friction points dragging each metric down, and validate hypotheses with real data before committing team time to a fix.
Design and implement fixes that compound, including shift-left quality changes, tooling investment, and better context and interfaces for both humans and agents, rather than one-off patches.
Stay hands-on enough to review architecture, dig into pipeline internals, and unblock the team on hard technical problems directly.

Internal Adoption & Non-Linear Productivity

Own a small set of high-impact friction areas as pathfinders, driving each from diagnosis through fix to measurable metric movement.
Work directly with affected engineering teams to ensure fixes are trusted, adopted, and don't quietly get reverted or worked around.
Track and report metric movement honestly, including when a bet didn't pay off.
Capture and codify reusable patterns and playbooks so that fixes validated by this team can be adopted org-wide with minimal friction.

Operations, Risk & Enablement

Set a cadence for reporting impact back to EM peers and leadership, framed around metric movement rather than activity.
Ensure the pilot's fixes degrade gracefully and don't introduce new reliability risk into CI/CD systems that other teams depend on.
Help define what "graduation" from pilot to permanent function looks like, and build the case (or the honest counter-case) based on results.

What You'll Bring

General

Track record leading small, high-autonomy engineering teams, ideally in developer productivity, CI/CD, platform, or infrastructure reliability, measured on system-level outcomes rather than feature delivery.
Deep comfort with CI/CD and build systems. You understand why pipelines flake, why they're slow, and what actually moves success-rate and latency numbers versus what just feels like progress.
Demonstrated root-cause instinct and a bar for talent over headcount: you'd rather run understaffed than fill a seat with someone good-enough.
Comfort operating under metrics-driven accountability, including publicly baselining a number and reporting honestly against it.
Strong executive-level communication. This pilot has direct visibility to engineering leadership.

Nice to have

Experience with agentic or AI-assisted development workflows, and a view on where human/agent friction shows up differently than pure human friction.
Prior experience running a defined-window pilot or 0 to 1 initiative with explicit success criteria.
Familiarity with GitLab's own CI/CD internals, or equivalent depth on another large-scale build/test system.

About The Role

Senior Engineering Managers at GitLab own outcomes for a defined engineering domain, build and grow the team that delivers them, and are trusted to operate with significant autonomy against a clear mandate.

This Senior Engineering Manager role focuses on driving non-linear productivity by building and leading a small, hand-picked team of engineers who find and fix the highest-leverage friction points in GitLab's own SDLC. Rather than incremental team management, this is a 0 to 1 team-building mandate. You will personally recruit 4 exceptional engineers, define how they work, and drive them through a root-cause, shift-left approach to engineering productivity, measured in system-level metrics (MRPM, pipeline success rate, pipeline latency), not story points or activity.

You will act as a bridge between the pilot squad, engineering managers whose teams are affected by friction points, and leadership, ensuring the team's fixes deliver durable, measurable value before any of it is proposed as a permanent function.

This role reports to a VP-level engineering leader.

What You'll Do

Vision & Strategy

Define and continuously refine the operating model for the non-linear productivity pilot: what "friction" means, how it's diagnosed, and how fixes are prioritized against the three system-level metrics.
Identify and prioritize non-linear productivity opportunities (step-change fixes rather than incremental gains) across the SDLC, including flaky tests, review latency, pipeline reliability, tooling gaps, and context loss for both human and agentic contributors.
Translate an intentionally broad, ambiguous mandate ("find the friction, fix it at the root") into a concrete, time-boxed roadmap with defined milestones for a 3-month pilot window.

Team Building & Leadership

Personally source, evaluate, and select 4 exceptional engineers for the pilot squad. You own this hiring bar directly rather than delegating it to a pipeline.
Negotiate allocation models (100% vs. partial/dual-hat) with each engineer's current EM, balancing team commitments against the pilot's needs.
Set the technical direction and working norms for a small, fast-moving team: how work is scoped, how decisions get made, and how progress gets reported.
Mentor the engineers on this team in root-cause diagnosis and shift-left thinking, raising the bar for rigor versus reaching for the nearest patch.

Deep Technical Exploration & Experimentation

Lead hands-on investigation to instrument and baseline the three top-level metrics (MRPM, pipeline success rate, pipeline latency) so the org has an honest starting point before any fix is proposed.
Diagnose the highest-leverage friction points dragging each metric down, and validate hypotheses with real data before committing team time to a fix.
Design and implement fixes that compound, including shift-left quality changes, tooling investment, and better context and interfaces for both humans and agents, rather than one-off patches.
Stay hands-on enough to review architecture, dig into pipeline internals, and unblock the team on hard technical problems directly.

Internal Adoption & Non-Linear Productivity

Own a small set of high-impact friction areas as pathfinders, driving each from diagnosis through fix to measurable metric movement.
Work directly with affected engineering teams to ensure fixes are trusted, adopted, and don't quietly get reverted or worked around.
Track and report metric movement honestly, including when a bet didn't pay off.
Capture and codify reusable patterns and playbooks so that fixes validated by this team can be adopted org-wide with minimal friction.

Operations, Risk & Enablement

Set a cadence for reporting impact back to EM peers and leadership, framed around metric movement rather than activity.
Ensure the pilot's fixes degrade gracefully and don't introduce new reliability risk into CI/CD systems that other teams depend on.
Help define what "graduation" from pilot to permanent function looks like, and build the case (or the honest counter-case) based on results.

General

Track record leading small, high-autonomy engineering teams, ideally in developer productivity, CI/CD, platform, or infrastructure reliability, measured on system-level outcomes rather than feature delivery.
Deep comfort with CI/CD and build systems. You understand why pipelines flake, why they're slow, and what actually moves success-rate and latency numbers versus what just feels like progress.
Demonstrated root-cause instinct and a bar for talent over headcount: you'd rather run understaffed than fill a seat with someone good-enough.
Comfort operating under metrics-driven accountability, including publicly baselining a number and reporting honestly against it.

Experience with agentic or AI-assisted development workflows, and a view on where human/agent friction shows up differently than pure human friction.

Job Description

This position is based in Abilene, TX and will require relocation if not already based in Abilene, TX.

As Director of Operations, Critical Infrastructure
, you will lead the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of mission-critical electrical, mechanical, and building infrastructure systems supporting OCI data center campuses. This role is accountable for day-to-day operational execution, risk management, maintenance performance, and leadership effectiveness across assigned sites or regions, ensuring compute load is protected and high availability is maintained at all times.

This role directly leads site-level operational leadership for critical infrastructure, including the Site Operations Support Manager – Data Center Facilities, Office & Facilities Coordinator – Facilities Operations, Facilities Operations Manager – Mechanical / Plant Manager, and Facilities Operations Manager – Electrical / Plant Manager, along with their supporting technical teams. The Director is responsible for ensuring these teams operate as one coordinated facilities organization with strong execution discipline, clear escalation paths, and consistent standards across maintenance, incident response, operational readiness, and support functions.

This is a hands-on operational leadership role with direct accountability for operational outcomes. You will partner closely with Engineering, Construction, Training, Vendor Management, Reliability, and Chief Engineering functions to operationalize standards, strengthen maintenance and emergency response programs, and ensure operability and maintainability are built into both current operations and future growth.

Responsibilities

Lead and manage site or regional operations teams responsible for critical infrastructure, including electrical distribution, on-site power generation, UPS, switchgear, cooling systems, controls interfaces, and life safety systems.
Provide leadership across the full site facilities operations structure, including plant operations, maintenance execution, administrative site support, and operational coordination functions.
Own operational readiness, maintenance execution, and incident response performance for assigned campuses or regions.
Enforce consistent execution and continuous improvement of MOPs, SOPs, and EOPs governing maintenance, load transfers, switching, ramp events, restoration, and abnormal operating conditions.
Ensure strong coordination between electrical, mechanical, and site-support functions so operational work is executed safely, efficiently, and in alignment with uptime expectations.
Serve as the operational escalation point for major incidents, ensuring timely response, clear communication, root cause rigor, and disciplined corrective action follow-through.
Establish and track operational KPIs related to availability, reliability, safety, maintenance effectiveness, backlog health, incident trends, and readiness.
Partner with training and technical leadership teams to implement and sustain repair, preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, and emergency response capability across site teams.
Lead vendor oversight and support performance management for OEMs, maintenance providers, service contractors, and operating agreements tied to campus infrastructure.
Drive a strong safety and compliance culture aligned with company standards and applicable regulatory requirements.
Support staffing, hiring, retention, and development of high-performing operations leaders and technical staff across the organization.
Ensure site-support and administrative functions enable effective scheduling, documentation, workflow coordination, and audit-ready operations in support of the critical environment.
Partner with Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, and Reliability teams to ensure operability, maintainability, and operational supportability are built into new capacity, retrofits, and expansions.
Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure maintenance, capital work, remediation, and operational activities are properly sequenced and executed with minimal operational risk.
Drive continuous improvement across maintenance practices, incident response, work control, readiness processes, and team operating rhythms.

Ideal Candidate Profile

10+ years of experience in mission-critical operations, power generation, utilities, industrial operations, or related uptime-critical environments, including leadership responsibility.
Strong understanding of critical MEP systems and data center operations, including the interaction between electrical, mechanical, controls, and support functions in live environments.
Demonstrated experience managing operational risk and executing in MOP-driven environments.
Proven ability to lead managers, technical teams, and vendor-supported operations in 24/7 critical environments.
Strong experience with maintenance governance, incident response, and operational readiness at site or regional scale.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Facilities, Operations, or related field preferred; equivalent experience also valued.

Skills And Competencies

Strong operational leadership in mission-critical environments.
Ability to lead through managers while reinforcing accountability, consistency, and execution discipline.
Strong judgment during incidents and abnormal operating conditions.
Strong communication and cross-functional leadership skills.
Ability to balance safety, speed, reliability, and long-term maintainability in a live operational environment.
Strong planning, escalation, and organizational leadership capability.
Ability to align plant operations, maintenance delivery, and site-support functions into a cohesive operating model.

Preferred Skills / Certifications

PE license or equivalent certification is a plus.
Experience with regulatory compliance frameworks such as OSHA, EPA, and related operational requirements.
Familiarity with CMMS, SCADA, BMS, EPMS, and power monitoring platforms.
Experience in hyperscale data centers, utility-scale power systems, or similarly complex high-availability environments is strongly preferred.
Experience partnering with Engineering, Construction, Reliability, and Training functions in support of large-scale infrastructure operations is preferred.

Physical Demands / Work Environment

This is a mission-critical onsite leadership role supporting 24/7 operations where continuous uptime is essential. Regular attendance, schedule flexibility, and availability during major operational events are required. To perform these duties, you must be able to move through office, campus, and active operational environments; walk sites; climb stairs; and safely engage in field visibility and incident support activities, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Why Oracle Cloud Infrastructure?

Global impact at scale:
Contribute directly to how mission-critical OCI data centers operate across regions and continents, influencing infrastructure reliability, security, sustainability, and long-term capacity growth.

Technically rigorous environment:
Work alongside experienced engineers, automation specialists, and compliance teams in a rapidly scaling hyperscale cloud infrastructure, where disciplined execution and technical depth matter.

Culture built on operational excellence:
Join an organization that values safety, process rigor, clear accountability, and continuous improvement as foundational to protecting uptime and customer trust.

Company Description

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Job Description

l

Role overview

The Global Director, Global Technology Partnerships leads the Partner Technology Architect (PTA) team across ServiceNow’s technology ecosystem; hyperscalers, ISVs, and strategic technology partnerships spanning every geography. As the persistent partner-facing technical authority within the Partner Technology Acceleration Group (PTAG), this leader turns platform and AI depth into co-innovation at scale across ServiceNow’s technology routes to market.

The role carries three accountabilities: accelerate adoption of ServiceNow’s full platform and AI portfolio through the technology-partner ecosystem; grow the paths to revenue that flow through the ServiceNow Store, co-sell, and partner-influenced motions; and build the architectural credibility that positions ServiceNow as the workflow engine of the enterprise AI market. It pairs deep technical leadership with business development accountability, architectural authority, and commercial impact in one seat.

Why this role matters

Technology partnerships sit at the highest-leverage, most complex edge of the ecosystem. Hyperscalers are partners and platforms at once, ISVs monetize their own intellectual property on top of ServiceNow, and frontier-AI and advisory partners move faster than any single motion can keep pace with. This leader sets the technical strategy that turns those relationships into repeatable, co-innovated solutions and gives the field a credible architecture to sell with. Without that technical authority, even the strongest partnerships produce integrations that never scale into revenue.

Key responsibilities

Ecosystem strategy and orchestration

Define and drive the technical strategy for ServiceNow’s technology-partner ecosystem across hyperscaler, ISV, and strategic technology partnerships, so cross-partner patterns compound into ecosystem-wide momentum.
Own the partner prioritization model weighing technical readiness, co-innovation intent, and customer pipeline alignment to focus PTA coverage where ServiceNow wins and grows.
Translate PTAG and GPC strategy into ecosystem execution across every geography.
Build repeatable, scalable enablement that extends the team’s reach beyond its own capacity—creating a reusable content payload for recruiting and onboarding ISV partners and for positioning hyperscaler as a route to market, then activating it through GEO SC leadership so field teams and partners can lead these opportunities independently rather than depending on the team for every engagement.

Technical authority and co-innovation

Lead the PTA team as the persistent technical authority for the ecosystem; technical discovery, architectural validation, and competitive positioning that accelerate partner-led opportunities.
Drive AI-first co-innovation with partners, applying ServiceNow reference architectures and design standards to shape joint solutions and repeatable offerings.
Accelerate partner-built solutions through the ServiceNow Store surfacing co-innovation opportunities, guiding certification-ready design, and coordinating go-to-market with partners.
Grow partner mindshare, consumption, and solution quality by evangelizing ServiceNow platform and AI capabilities across the partner community.

Executive partnership management

Serve as the named ServiceNow technical counterpart to VP- and SVP-level leadership at each strategic technology partner.
Represent ServiceNow’s platform and AI strategy at partner executive forums, joint steering committees, and industry events.
Build trusted-advisor relationships with partner C-suite (CTO, CAIO, CDO) to shape practice investment and platform adoption roadmaps.
Navigate coexist-and-compete dynamics where a partner may be collaborator, platform, and customer at once.

Team leadership and talent

Build, inspire, and develop the global PTA team, establishing clear career paths, succession plans, and talent pipelines to support ecosystem growth.
Establish the operating model; engagement cadences, reporting rhythms, and knowledge-sharing practices that keep a distributed team aligned.
Drive recruiting for senior partner-facing technical talent, sourcing from platform companies, hyperscalers, and advanced consultancies.
Foster a PTA community of practice that turns cross-partner learning into collective technical strength.

Qualifications

15+ years in technology leadership spanning pre-sales, solution consulting, solution architecture, or technical partnership management at enterprise scale, with demonstrated success in partner-ecosystem contexts.
10+ years of second-line leadership building and scaling front-line technical teams across diverse geographies, with strong coaching and talent development.
Deep technical credibility across enterprise platforms, cloud architectures, and the AI stack—foundation models, agentic architectures, AI governance, and enterprise AI adoption patterns—with the ability to translate capability into business value.
Fluency in technology-partner go-to-market: hyperscaler co-sell, ISV and marketplace economics, and strategic technology alliances, including their business models and co-innovation requirements.
Proven track record growing partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue through measurable pipeline growth, deal velocity, and win-rate impact.
Executive presence to engage C-level partner stakeholders, present to large audiences, and build strategic relationships across organizational boundaries.
Experience leading distributed, high-autonomy technical teams across multiple geographies.

Preferred Qualifications

ServiceNow platform and AI portfolio experience, or deep familiarity with enterprise SaaS platforms and workflow automation.
Experience building or scaling partner marketplace or Store programs at a major technology platform.
Hyperscaler co-sell experience across public cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud).
Co-innovation framework or design-thinking expertise.
Background in developer relations, partner engineering, or technology alliance program management.

Location and travel

Global, with approximately 40–50% travel across partner sites, ServiceNow offices, and joint customer engagements.

, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure.
